title: [BUG] Cannot run after install - "cannot load library"
body:
## Bug Description
I get an error when I attempt to run kokoro-tts after installation of requirements

## Steps to Reproduce
I attempt to run the following from the kokoro-tts directory with a conda environment activated. The environment was activated when I installed the requirements.

`./kokoro-tts test.txt`


## Expected Behavior
kokoro-tts to do it's thing and generate the wav

## Actual Behavior
I get this Error:


`Traceback (most recent call last):  
  File "/home/myuser/progs/kokoro-tts/./kokoro-tts", line 20, in <module>  
    import sounddevice as sd  
  File "/home/myuser/miniconda3/envs/kokoro/lib/python3.12/site-packages/sounddevice.py", line 72, in <module>  
    _lib = _ffi.dlopen(_libname)  
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^  
OSError: cannot load library 'libportaudio.so.2': /home/myuser/miniconda3/envs/kokoro/bin/../lib/libstdc++.so.6: version 'GLIBCXX_3.4.32' not found (required by /lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libjack.so.0)`

## Environment
- OS: mint 22.1
- Python version: 3.12.9
- Voice model version: kokoro-v1.0.onnx
- Input format: TXT
author: StoryHack

comments.body:
I did get it working after I ran:

`conda install -c conda-forge libstdcxx-ng`

while having the conda environment activated. Not sure if something in the requirements needs to be updated.

your process is loading an older version of libstdc++ in this case, the copy inside your conda environment, that lacks the symbol version GLIBCXX_3.4.32 required by a system library (here, libjack.so.0). In other words, the version of the C++ standard library bundled with your conda environment is too old for the jack library on your system.

Install a newer version from conda-forge 
```
conda install -c conda-forge libstdcxx-ng
```

this (which you have already done) should fix your issue. its not a `kokoro-tts`  bug

comments.body:
i'm not entirely sure what you are trying to achieve, but you can pipe raw text into kokoro-tts STDIN

```bash
echo "I'm reading something that's not stored on a file" | ./kokoro-tts /dev/stdin output.wav
```

Sorry my fault. I should have been more consice yes it is possible by your method but it is extremely slow for batch generation. 
with gpu it produced 44 minute audio in 6 minutes 
but if I do it with your way it produces one file per second soo as soon as I want to do a 17000 lines it would take me straight up around 5 hours

For anyone having same problem as me run use multithreading feature of multoprocessing it helped I basically ran 12 instances of kokoro simultaneously
my script.py
```
import os
import sys
import subprocess
import multiprocessing

# Configuration
kokoro_tts_path = "./kokoro-tts"  # Adjust if needed
output_dir = os.path.expanduser("~/path/")  # Ensure this path exists
num_workers = 12  # Number of parallel processes

def synthesize_text(args):
    text, output_path = args
    print(f"Processing: {output_path}")
    try:
        subprocess.run(
            [kokoro_tts_path, "/dev/stdin", output_path, "--voice", "af_bella"],
            input=text.encode("utf-8"),
            check=True
        )
    except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
        print(f"Error processing {output_path}: {e}")

def batch_synthesize(input_file, output_file, workers=num_workers):
    # Read input texts and output filenames
    with open(input_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        lines = [line.strip() for line in f.readlines() if line.strip()]

    with open(output_file, "r", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        filenames = [line.strip() for line in f.readlines() if line.strip()]

    if len(lines) != len(filenames):
        print("Error: Input and output files must have the same number of lines.")
        sys.exit(1)

    tasks = [(text, os.path.join(output_dir, f"{filename}.wav")) for text, filename in zip(lines, filenames)]

    # Use multiprocessing to run tasks in parallel
    with multiprocessing.Pool(workers) as pool:
        pool.map(synthesize_text, tasks)

    print("Batch processing completed!")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    if len(sys.argv) != 3:
        print("Usage: python kokoro-inator.py <input_text_file> <output_names_file>")
        sys.exit(1)

    input_text_file = sys.argv[1]
    output_names_file = sys.argv[2]

    batch_synthesize(input_text_file, output_names_file)
```
run by 
```python script.py input.txt output.txt```
where input contains lines to voice 
output contains name to save as
